'''Ashain''' officially the '''Republic of Ashain,''' is an island country in west [[Quia]]. Located between the [[Haanian Ocean|Haanian]] and [[Great Hinsakian Ocean|Great Hinsakian]] oceans off the south and north coasts of the mainland, respectively, it is bordered to the east by the [[Ashanian Sea]] and borders [[Ahokini]]. The island of [[Island of Ashain|Ashain]] and the [[Asstia archipelago]] consists which consists of over [[Islands of Ashain|10,000 smaller islands]], covering [[List of countries and dependencies by area|422,225 square kilometres (163,022 sq mi)]]. Divided into [[Ashani prefectures|17 prefectures]] and [[Ashani island territories|13 island territories]], around three-quarters of the country's terrain is [[wikipedia:Mountain|mountainous]] and [[wikipedia:Forest|heavily forested]], concentrating its [[wikipedia:Agriculture|agriculture]] and highly urbanised population along its [[wikipedia:Coastal plain|coastal plains]]. With a population of over [[List of countries and dependencies by population|62 million]] as of 1765, it is the [[List of countries and dependencies by population|26th most populous country]]. The country's capital and largest city is [[Sjoran]].

The first known habitation of the [[Asstia archipelago|archipelago]] dates to the [[Pre-History Period]], dating to around 45,000 BFA. Between the 1st and 3rd centuries, its islands were slowly colonised by the [[Kingdom of Mara]] to the east, and later by the first dynasty of [[Naqhola dynasty|Naqhola]]. From the 10th century, the [[wikipedia:Aristocracy (class)|aristocracy]] would elect the [[Tlalori Law|successor from the rulers' children]]. After being ruled by the [[Esnanan dynasty|Esnanan]], [[Takayoran dynasty|Takayoran]] and [[Saekon dynasty|Saekon]] Dynasties, the last dynasty of [[Kuwana dynasty|Kuwana]] implemented an [[wikipedia:Expansionism| expansionist foreign policy]]. In 1597, after the death of [[Cuayasu]], his son [[Tlalko]] curtailed the power of the [[wikipedia:Aristocracy (class)|aristocracy]]. In the [[Cuami period]], Ashain pursued [[wikipedia:Industrialisation|Industrialization]] and [[wikipedia:Modernization theory|modernization]] as well as [[wikipedia:Militarism|militarism]] and [[wikipedia:Colonization|overseas colonization]]. The country set up colones across [[Acrola]], [[Quia]] and [[Mahea]].  They attacked [[Emara]] and [[Pelugrotoa]] after decade of tension, thus entering the [[Red War]] as an ___ power. After being defeated in [[Quia]] and [[Pelugrotoa]] and suffering the [[1693 Ashani famine]], Ashain surrendered in 1694. Afterward, the country underwent slow economic growth and became one of the five earliest major allies of [[Dahe]]. Since its exit from the [[Quian union]] in 1647, it has experienced a prolonged period of [[wikipedia:Geopolitics| geopolitical]] uncertainty.

Ashain is a [[wikipedia:Unitary state|unitary]] [[wikipedia:Presidential system|presidential republic]] with a [[wikipedia:Bicameralism|bicameral legislature]] known as the [[Ashani National Diet|National Diet]]. It maintains one of the world's strongest [[wikipedia:Navy navies]] but has constitutionally renounced its right to [[wikipedia:Declaration of war|declare war]] unless (though this is soon going to be removed). It has one of the lowest [[List of countries by unemployment rate|unemployment rates]] in the world, with a reported rate of 1% in the first quarter of 1758. This is due to a large proportion of the population working part-time in subsistence agriculture, typically to support their parents (own-account work and unpaid family work). Ashain enjoys a [[List of countries by Krali Total Development Index|very high standard of living,]] safety, and [[wikipedia:Economic_freedom|economic freedom]], as well as free [[wikipedia:University| University]] and [[wikipedia:Universal health care|universal health care]]. The wider culture of Elaian is well known globally, especially its popular culture, which includes art, cuisine, films, music, and board games.

== Economy ==
Main article: [[Economy of Ashain]]

=== Agriculture and Fishery ===
Agriculture, aquaculture, and fishing combined represents 5.5% percent of the Ashaini economy as a portion of GDP<ref>cite some World Bank type thing</ref>, though most of that portion consists of the fishing sector. Agriculture remains a minor part of the Ashaini economy, as only a small portion of the land is arable. Despite state-led efforts to increase national agricultural self-sufficiency, only X% of Ashaini land remains arable, and the country has a 21.2% agricultural self-sufficiency rate<ref>cite some government report on autarky</ref>. Ashaini agriculture primarily produces rice and grain, with a middling crop yield per square kilometre. 

Fishing remains as a significant part of the Ashani economy and represents a considerable supplement to the Ashani diet. Ashain is the fourth largest catcher of fish in the world, catching 3.5 million metric tonnes of fish in the year 1761<ref>cite some statistics looking thing</ref>, and the second largest consumer of fish per capita<ref>cite the same statistics thing</ref>. 

The government maintains small but consistent subsidies and strong protections to the agricultural industry of the nation<ref>cite a government budget report</ref>. Additionally, Ashain has a small but vigorous agricultural science sector, producing the 3rd highest number of agricultural patents per capita<ref>cite the same budget report</ref>. 

=== Manufacturing ===
Ashain has a considerable industrial capacity, and is home to some of the globe's more dominant chemical, ships, electronics, machine tools, and steel sectors. Out of these, Ashain is most notable for its shipbuilding sector, accounting for 19% of global shipbuilding capacity<ref>cite that OECD thing or maybe a government source. Maybe a country wide shipbuilding data collection thing</ref>. Its industry makes up of about 37.1% of GDP<ref>government finances report</ref>, and its value-added output is the 14th highest in the world<ref>same statistia thnig</ref>. 

Ashain maintains one of the world's leading shipbuilding sectors, only overtaken by [[Dahe]] and [[Raledria]] in terms of shipbuilding capacity<ref>cite a shipbuilding sector report</ref>. It is the third largest in output<ref>cite the same report</ref>, but also the second largest in terms of commercial orders<ref>cite a global shipbuilding report</ref>. Though the sector faces increasing competition from neighbours, it nevertheless remains as a major sector of the economy and a strong focus of the government, being the highest receiver of state subsidies and loans and consisting of 14.1% of the nation's GDP<ref>cite a government budget responsibility report for the first thing</ref><ref>cite a government financial report, the one from earlier.</ref>.
